title: React Introduction
summary: React builds a web page from small parts called components. Meet a simple component and a button that remembers clicks.
introduction: A toy house can be made from lots of small blocks. React helps you make a web page from small parts too. Each part is called a component. Start with a greeting, then use it twice. These examples need a React project; they do not run in this site's plain JavaScript playground.
learningObjectives: Explain what a React component does
Pass a name into a component
Read a button that remembers how many times it was clicked

blocks.text: React is a JavaScript **library**: a set of helpful tools for building the parts people see and use. A component is a function that describes one of those parts. The next lesson shows how to create a React project.

blocks.title: A greeting component

blocks.content: The page shows a main heading: Hello, coder!

blocks.text: `Greeting` is the component name. `return` gives back what it should show. The HTML-like part is called **JSX**. A build tool turns JSX into JavaScript that a browser can run.

blocks.title: Two greetings from one component

blocks.text: `name` is a **prop**: a value passed into a component. Curly brackets let JSX use a JavaScript value. We use the same component twice, but give it two different names.

blocks.title: A button that counts

blocks.content:
At first: Clicks: 0
After one click: Clicks: 1

items: **State** is a value a component remembers.
`onClick` says what to do when the button is clicked.
React shows the new count after it changes.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Start component names with a capital letter, such as `Greeting`. React uses that capital to tell your component apart from a normal HTML tag such as `p`.

React helps with the page parts. It does not include every tool an app might need. For example, switching between page addresses often uses another library, such as React Router. You can learn that later.

blocks.title: Your turn
blocks.text: Read the counter without running it. What will the button say after three clicks? Change the first value from 0 to 5. What will it say after one click now?

seo.title: React Introduction – What React Is and Is Not
seo.description: Learn what React is, how declarative components differ from imperative DOM code, what React leaves to other libraries, and which React 19 features matter.
